title: Snapshot Stripline Explorer — model variant latency & token economics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable ‘Snapshot Stripline Explorer’ for per-model and per-route views that surfaces short-term latency shifts, token-cost drift, and model-variant regressions in a single horizontal strip. The component should be usable inside the Route Overview and Model Variant pages and act as a lightweight alternative to the full Performance Canvas when users need a quick triage.

Scope:
- Small horizontal card (280x72px) containing: 95th/median latency mini-sparkline, throughput sparkbar, token-per-request micro-gauge, and a cost-drift mini-thermometer.
- Two interaction levels: hover to expand to a 320x140px overlay with short timeline (24h) and top-3 contributing traces; click to open Route Performance panel.
- Variant-aware: visualizes up to three model variants (baseline, canary, fallback) with configurable color stacking.

Non-goals: full trace viewer, long-range historical analytics, or replacing the Performance Canvas. This is intended for quick operator triage and rollout decisions.
design_notes: Use three distinct hues derived from the Console palette: teal-500 (baseline), amber-500 (canary), gray-600 (fallback). Ensure 3:1 contrast against background for accessibility.
Latency visualization: combined sparkline for median + 95th percentile overlay; 95th shown as thicker line with subtle shadow to emphasize tail risk.
Throughput: tiny vertical sparkbars behind latency sparkline to hint at request volume; bars are low-opacity to avoid clutter.
Token gauge: circular micro-gauge (24px) showing average tokens/request with numeric label on hover; color shifts when tokens drift >10% from baseline.
Cost drift: linear mini-thermometer showing percent delta vs baseline; red gradient capped at +40% to avoid visual domination.
Interaction: hover expansion reveals short list of top 3 traces (sampling keys) and quick action buttons: Open Route, Start Canary, Rollback Variant.
Performance tradeoffs: limit mini-sparkline to 24h with 1m granularity to keep payload small; recommend server-side pre-aggregation endpoint (ENG-98123).
Fallback states: empty state shows ‘no data’ micro-copy and a lightweight CTA linking to ‘Enable telemetry’ guide; error state surfaces a warning icon and retry affordance.
Animation: micro-animations limited to 120ms fade/translate on hover to stay below perceived latency threshold.
Localization: numeric formats must respect locale and use significant-digit abbreviation (e.g., 1.2k tokens).
Accessibility: all interactive elements keyboard-focusable; expanded overlay must be dismissible with ESC and announce via ARIA roles.
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created. Initial concept sketch and PRD linked. Archived early sketches in design folder.
2025-02-21: Low-fidelity prototype uploaded to Figma (frame A). Shared with PM and Eng for feasibility check — ENG flagged pre-aggregation requirement.
2025-02-25: Design crit with Console UX team. Feedback: reduce visual density, make token gauge optional in compact routes list, prefer overlay for trace details.
2025-02-27: Incorporated crit: token gauge becomes a toggle; interaction updated to hover->expand then click->panel open. Updated figma link attached.
2025-03-01: Engineering feasibility sync — ENG-98123 created to add pre-aggregation endpoint; noted cost implications for per-route high-cardinality telemetry.
2025-03-03: UX review scheduled with product leadership. Need follow-up on rollout action semantics (Start Canary vs Canary-only route) from PM (PM-412).
acceptance_criteria: Compact strip renders in Route list and Model Variant pages without layout shift at default density.
Hover expansion shows 24h mini-timeline and top-3 traces sampled; trace items link to Performance panel.
Color-coding for variants matches Console palette and passes WCAG AA contrast for text overlays.
Token gauge toggle available in Route list settings and persists per-user via console prefs.
Design handoff includes annotated Figma frames, CSS tokens, and interaction specs; frontend PR implements ARIA roles and keyboard flows.
Performance budget: component payload must not increase route-list API response by more than 15% if telemetry pre-aggregation is enabled.
mockups: Figma frame B: expanded hover overlay
Figma frame C: empty + error states
ux_tasks: Produce CSS token spec for palette and token gauge sizes
Deliver exportable SVG assets for sparkbars and thermometers
Add keyboard/ARIA interaction notes to handoff file
notes_for_engineering: Request pre-aggregated 24h tiles at 1m granularity from telemetry (ENG-98123).
Provide toggle flag for token gauge per-user; store in preferences endpoint.
Front-end should sample up to 3 variants; server to cap payload and return ordered variant metrics.
If telemetry endpoint is unavailable, component should degrade to showing last-known snapshot with an info tooltip.
estimated_kpis: Mean time to triage reduced by ~20% in routes with Snapshot Stripline enabled (target).
Heat-detection rate for regressions (alerts acknowledged within 1 hour) increase by 12% (hypothesis).
